questions.stem: A team writes one criterion, "replies should be accurate". Which addition turns it into something an eval can enforce?

options.text: A monthly review where the team reads sample replies
options.says: Ruled out because a review is a process and does not make the criterion measurable: "Nobody can say what number or scale a result would have".

options.text: A target that sets a metric, a threshold and a data set
options.says: A good criterion names "a metric, a threshold, a data set, and a baseline to beat", and the four traits ask for "quantitative metrics or well-defined qualitative scales".

options.text: A longer list that spells out the qualities of a good reply
options.says: Ruled out because a longer list of qualities repeats the problem, since good, accurate and natural are "wishes until they carry a number or a scale and a data set".

options.text: A ranking that puts accuracy ahead of speed and cost
options.says: Ruled out because the page says "Most use cases need multidimensional evaluation along several success criteria", which means a number for each, not one ranking in a sentence.

origin.section: Four traits of a good criterion

questions.stem: A ticket-routing prompt is edited, and the team reruns a set in which every case is graded by a script. Which grader fits a case whose output must parse as a JSON object holding a `queue` key?

options.text: A pattern check that finds the word queue in the output
options.says: Ruled out because a pattern "is found anywhere in the output", so it would pass text that does not parse as one JSON object.

options.text: An exact match against one stored reference output
options.says: Ruled out because exact match decides "A categorical answer: a label, a choice", and a whole reference output would fail on key order or an extra field.

options.text: A structure check that decodes and compares the value
options.says: The page lists a "Structure check" for "A reply that must parse and carry the right fields", and says it "parses the whole output as JSON".

options.text: A similarity score against a reference output
options.says: Ruled out because similarity answers "Whether two texts say the same thing", and a queue name has an exact right value.

origin.section: Pick the cheapest grader that can tell the difference

questions.stem: A prompt change scores better overall, and the team wants to be sure the improvement is real before launch. Which pair of checks gives the most trustworthy answer?

options.text: A comparison per case, and a second run of the same cases
options.says: Ruled out because rerunning the same cases repeats the tuned set, and "The score is then a memory test".

options.text: A review of the average, and a run on held-out cases
options.says: Ruled out because a review of the average cannot show a rare failure, and "An average never excuses a regression".

options.text: A larger set of the same easy cases, and a stricter threshold
options.says: Ruled out because "Grading only what is easy to grade" measures a different task, and a threshold on easy cases does not change that.

options.text: A comparison per case, and a run on held-out cases
options.says: The page says "Compare per case" and to "Keep a held-out slice that the loop never touches and run it at the end".

questions.stem: A case passes in two of three repeated runs. How should the harness treat it?

options.text: A pass, because two of three runs succeeded
options.says: Ruled out because a case that fails sometimes will fail for some customers, which is why "a flaky case is a finding".

options.text: A fail, listed as flaky in the report
options.says: The page says to "pass it only if every run passes", and that "A case that passes in some runs and fails in others is flaky".

options.text: A pass, once the failing run is discarded
options.says: Ruled out because discarding the failing run removes the evidence, and the page says to "pass it only if every run passes".

options.text: A fail, left out of the count of flaky cases
options.says: Ruled out because the criteria "can say how many flaky cases are tolerated", which needs the count to include it.
